exercises.prompt: What is the grammatical difference between هٰذَا كِتَابٌ and هٰذَا الكِتَابُ?
choices: هٰذَا كِتَابٌ is a complete sentence ('This is a book'); هٰذَا الكِتَابُ is a noun phrase ('this book')
هٰذَا الكِتَابُ is a complete sentence; هٰذَا كِتَابٌ is a phrase
exercises.answer: هٰذَا كِتَابٌ is a complete sentence ('This is a book'); هٰذَا الكِتَابُ is a noun phrase ('this book')
exercises.explanation: A demonstrative + noun with the definite article (الـ) forms a single noun phrase; a demonstrative + indefinite noun forms a complete nominal sentence.

feedback.rule: Demonstrative + definite noun = phrase; demonstrative + indefinite noun = sentence.

exercises.prompt: Select the correct near demonstrative for a non-human broken plural ('these books').
exercises.explanation: Non-human plurals take feminine singular agreement, so use هٰذِهِ (not هٰؤُلَاءِ, which is for humans).

feedback.rule: Non-human plurals take feminine singular demonstratives (هٰذِهِ / تِلْكَ).

exercises.prompt: Arrange the words to form: 'This book is useful.'
exercises.explanation: هٰذَا الكِتَابُ forms the definite subject phrase, followed by the indefinite predicate مُفِيدٌ.
